answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, like a willow bending without breaking under load. The stake is slashed if the agent is caught faking identity, so an attacker spawning a river of fake agents must fund every single one, and the cost multiplies with each copy. Honest agents keep a small ember of reputation that grows with verified work, letting them transact cheaply, while fresh identities start at zero trust and pay higher fees until they prove themselves.
